Taylor Farms - the produce giant whose lettuce has been recalled in connection
with the "explosive diarrhea" outbreak sweeping the United States - and its
lobbying groups have for years worked to end or delay programs meant to help
the government better test for foodborne diseases and prevent their spread,
according to records reviewed by **Zeteo**.

Over a decade ago, Taylor Farms and big agricultural industry groups
[successfully](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CHRG-111hhrg52327/html/CHRG-111hhrg52327.htm)
[lobbied](https://web.archive.org/web/20111024003705/http://www.ams.usda.gov/AMSv1.0/getfile?dDocName=STELPRDC5090885)
to
[defund](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BUDGET-2013-CCS/pdf/BUDGET-2013-CCS.pdf)
a significant foodborne illness testing program that was responsible for some
80% of U.S. public produce pathogen testing.

More recently, under Donald Trump's second administration, a lobbying group
that Taylor Farms belongs to successfully
[pushed](https://www.congress.gov/118/chrg/CHRG-118shrg50503/CHRG-118shrg50503.pdf)
to delay a rule that would have helped the government more quickly trace
contaminations back to specific locations - which could have helped prevent
the illness at hand, cyclosporiasis, from proliferating into thousands of
cases nationwide.

The Trump administration [moved](https://www.fda.gov/food/hfp-constituent-
updates/fda-intends-extend-compliance-date-food-traceability-rule) to delay
the tracing rule last year. Several days later, Taylor Farms
[donated](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/fecimg/?202507319789366251) $1
million to a pro-Trump super PAC. That summer, Taylor Farms
[contributed](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/fecimg/?202510279792025569)
another $1 million to House Republicans' super PAC, and a few months later,
Republicans in Congress [enshrined](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-
congress/house-bill/5371/text) the rule delay as part of a funding bill.

Separately, legal
[complaints](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.caed.255594/gov.uscourts.caed.255594.101.0_1.pdf)
and employee [accounts](https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Taylor-Farms-
Reviews-E1010102.htm) suggest that Taylor Farms's facilities have been host to
unsanitary workplace conditions, with staff working long hours and receiving
sparse breaks - conditions that experts say could foster the spread of
foodborne illnesses.
